steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line baking sheets with parchment paper.
Mix peanut butter, white sugar, and egg in a medium bowl until smooth.
Roll mixture into 1-inch balls and place 1 inch apart on an ungreased baking sheet; flatten each with a fork, making a criss-cross pattern.

Bake in the preheated oven until cookies are just barely brown on the bottoms, about 6 to 8 minutes. They can become too crumbly if they are overcooked. Cool on the baking sheets briefly before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Three Ingredient Peanut Butter Cookies
raw_recipe.description: Easy peanut butter cookies made with three ingredients: creamy peanut butter, sugar, and an egg. Great for kids learning to bake and ready in minutes!

video.description: Peanut butter cookies have never been so easy-to-make. In this video, learn how to make three-ingredient peanut butter cookies with Allrecipes! Perfect for a rainy or cold night indoors, these homemade cookies practically melt in your mouth and can be made in under 15 minutes!

review.reviewBody: I read the reviews for this recipe before I made them. I figured with so little ingredients try them and if they aren't good I am not out too much. I rolled them into large walnut shaped balls and pressed a fork with sugar in a crosscut pattern. I baked them for almost 15 minutes and they did not burn. I asked Husband to rate them. For him it was a definite 10. I then proceeded to ask each our our four sons who also gave it a 10. After the first batch I decided to flatten them more and sprinkle with sugar. They cooked much quicker. I have found with this cookie cook them till the top turns slightly white. let them cool for 5 minutes then transfer to plate or platter. Ours made 20 cookies. I ended up making another batch a little later in the evening and made a BIG cookie with chocolate chips pressed into the cookie. It made 1 pizza pan sized cookie. Thanks for the great and easy Recipe. I will definitely make this one again.

Great cookies! I added a splash of vanilla, a small pinch of baking soda and a little salt and they turned out delicious. Without the additions, they tasted a little off. With the baking soda, the cookies really spread out! I also baked them for a total of 12 minutes this time around, and found that I liked them better this way.

Great and easy recipe to makes. A tablespoon of all purpose flour is necessary as the dough is too sticky and gooey without it. Flour helps firm it up and makes it easy to handle to shape into balls. Only a tablespoon is needed. It’s enough to make it to where it can be handled, but doesn’t make the cookies crumbly in the end. Also, 8 minutes was not enough time to bake them. They were still soft and doughy after 8 minutes. I had to bake them for 10 minutes to get them right. You really want to be careful to not over bake these. They have a nice, rich flavor and I would highly recommend this recipe to everyone as it’s easy and only has 3 ingredients. It’s the perfect recipe for someone who is beginning to learn how to bake. It’s also great to do with your kids as it’s such a simple recipe. Highly recommended!

I loved these cookies! I made these for my family and they were absolutely delicious, although I did make some changes to the recipe to make them more unique. I am only 23 years old, and while I am a bit gifted in baking, I think these were very easy and with assistance and supervision, even a toddler could help make these! First, I leveled off my peanut butter and sugar with a steak knife, the flat edged side. Second, I used two less tablespoons of white sugar and in their place, I used three tablespoons of golden yellow sugar. I find it just gives it a more special, caramelized flavor. Second, I used Kraft-brand extra roasted peanut butter (I live on the East Coast, but I think any other brand will do as long as it is not all-natural peanut butter). Then, I used a spatula to mix it all together. Instead of roughly scooping it out, I used my one tablespoon measuring spoon to scoop out the dough and used my finger and thumb to level off the excess on top. I rolled it between my palms and put them on my extra-large cookie sheet, (a regular one will do) and I didn't even need parchment paper! I baked them at 350 for 9 minutes (I tried taking them out at 6 minutes and it was still raw, my thumb in my oven mitt made an indent into one, so I put them in for another three minutes) and I waited until my cookie sheet had fully cooled down to take them off of the sheet. I had to do them in two batches for the remaining six balls of cookie dough. I did the first batch in rows, the top row being five balls of dough, the second being four balls of dough, the third being five balls of dough again and the bottom row being four balls of dough. These were amazing, so simple and I will make them again!

I added 2 tablespoons of Dutch process cocoa powder and 1 teaspoon of vanilla. I just baked them as balls instead of pressing them out and topped them with a little coarse salt and chocolate syrup. This is so simple and yet so delicious. I found this rich and delicious and I will use it again, even if just as a base.

Perfect recipe when you’re low on ingredients at home, but still want something yummy to make with the kids. For reference I used my ninja foodi grill oven thing. The first batch I followed the instructions. It was way too soft to take out at 8 min so I left it in until it browned a bit on top and it was still soft, but able to be moved to a rack. Once cooled, it was perfect cookie texture. The second batch I took someone’s advice below and added a pinch of baking soda, vanilla, I omitted the salt because my peanut butter is already salty, and added mini marshmallows. Cooked for 12 min this time and it was perfect! The kids loved it so much. Thank you for this recipe! It’s a perfect base for adding into also.

I'm obsessed with these. They're even better than doing it the "real way," with flour and butter and all that jazzeroo. I added a tsp of vanilla & baking powder, and chilled the dough for 30 minutes for better consistency. I also add a hershey kiss in the middle of each cookie after they come out of the oven, before they set. They won't look done when you take them out, but just wait like 10 minutes for them to cool! My gluten-free friends all worship me now for introducing these :) I love that they're low-effort, but still amazing.
P.S. I've had bad luck with dark pans and letting the oven get hotter than 350. Cookies get really flat and caramelized.

If you make small changes to this recipe you end up with a fabulous cookie you need three to four tablespoons of flour a quarter teaspoon of vanilla and a pinch of salt cook for 10 minutes and they turn out wonderful if you don't add the flour they're to gooey and not rollable 24 normal size cookies or 32 button size cookies I added white chocolate chips to some of them on top delicious

I made this after I made another one of your peanut butter cookie recipes. It had more ingredients than this one. I really like this one too. Even more soft. I altered it by doubling the ingredients with one cup of sugar and one cup of brown sugar. I got close to 40 cookies from it!! I did eight minutes for the full recommended time. I think if I did a minute more would've been ok too just because of how super soft they are.

I made as directed, though I doubled the recipe and used a 15oz jar of Jiff Chocolate Peanut Butter, put on small baking pan for bar cookies...let me tell you, these are the best EVER...I used my mixer baked at 350 for 15-20 min more of a brownie texture absolutely delicious 😋

I followed the advice of the commenters and added 1 TBSP flour, pinch salt, 1/2 tsp. baking soda and 1/2 TBSP vanilla. Flavour on point, over baked the first batch (crumbled), but reduced 1 minute (for a total of 12 minutes) and second batch were perfect.
These cookies came out way too gooey for my liking. Was hoping for a much crunchier cookie. Perhaps cooking it longer would help but as per present recipe instructions this cookie is a pass for me.
Very simple but the results are a long way from the classic Pb cookie texture and flavour I was hoping for. Ok if you absolutely need a GF option but I wouldn't make them again.
Yummy followed the recipe
Easy to make and great taste!!
Made it with 3/4 cup stevia brown sugar. They were very good and a great diabetic friendly snack. Chilling dough first makes rolling into balls easier and less sticky.

Um so basically when I was cooking them I checked every 3 minutes or so and they ne ver seemed cooked and after around 10-15 minutes of resetting the timer I decided to take them out. When I tested them with a knife just to see if they were cooked they completely fell. The texture of them after being in the oven for 15 minutes was almost the same as the batter. I added in a sprinkle of bak9ing soda for good measure like many of the reviews recommended but that didn't seem to do anything. After cooking for 20 minutes I took them out and let them sit and they solidified and were way less soft and mushy. overall not a bad recipe, they just got the timing wrong

Very easy, and I substituted white sugar with coconut sugar and then cut it down to half a cup of sugar, so it was a little healthier. Very, very easy and quick! I now make them almost weekly. My husband doesn’t usually like peanut butter cookies but he likes these!
Easy
Baked for 15 minutes per other reviews and came out beautiful, chewy and crispy. Keeping this recipe!
